commands.name: ChangeTaskRelationship
input: reason_category required for unlink and absent/null for link
preflight: require canonical UUIDv4 task_id and target_id, positive integer task_revision (boolean rejected), relationship_kind exactly sr|rfc|device and action exactly link|unlink
unlink requires nonempty one-line reason_category of 1..128 UTF-8 bytes with no NUL/CR/LF; link requires reason_category absent/null so ignored caller text cannot alter replay semantics
COMMAND_ENVELOPE_V1 binds task_id/relationship_kind/target_id/action/reason_category and carries task_revision as the exact Task base revision
steps: inside one writer UnitOfWork load the exact Task; missing returns TASK_NOT_FOUND and revision mismatch returns TASK_STALE before receipt/domain mutation

revalidate target identity existence against the owning LLD-03 identity table selected only from the closed relationship_kind registry: service_requests.service_request_id, rfcs.rfc_id, or device_references.device_reference_id; missing target returns TASK_RELATIONSHIP_TARGET_NOT_FOUND

require sr/rfc relationships to target a Local Task; WFM direct SR/RFC requests return TASK_RELATIONSHIP_INVALID because WFM SR/RFC context derives only through its owning RFC; device is valid for Local or WFM
load the exact current active relationship row for task_id+kind+target_id under the writer lock

for link, an already-active exact pair is semantic NO_CHANGE after exact Task/target freshness; for unlink, absence of an active exact pair is semantic NO_CHANGE after exact Task/target freshness, whether the pair was previously closed or never existed; NO_CHANGE inserts no receipt child, relationship history or audit and advances no revision
material link inserts the receipt, allocates a new link_id and inserts a new active relationship row; a prior closed row is never reactivated, reused or rewritten

material unlink inserts the receipt then guarded-updates only the exact active link row from active=1/closed_command_id=NULL to active=0/closed_command_id=command_id; link identity, task, target and opened_command_id remain unchanged and the closed row is thereafter immutable

every material direct relationship change increments tasks.revision exactly once, including WFM Device Reference link/unlink; no target revision, RFC hierarchy/source revision, Objective revision or membership revision changes

audit one task.relationship_changed.v1 event: relationship_kind=sr|rfc|device, action maps link->OPEN and unlink->CLOSE, relationship_id is the new/opened or exact closed link_id, related_id=target_id, prior_related_id=null, resulting_revision is the resulting Task revision, reason_category=null for OPEN and the accepted unlink reason for CLOSE; result refs contain that task_relationship identity
commit atomically; CommandBoundary replay resolves before owner-state reads and returns the original immutable result without reopening/reclosing a relationship
rules: target revisions are deliberately not freshness inputs: Service Request/RFC/Device Reference relational identities are immutable and direct relationship validity does not depend on mutable descriptive text, RFC hierarchy role, RFC archive/presentation state, source lifecycle, or Device regularization state; existence is revalidated inside the writer UoW
Local Task RFC relationship may target root or subordinate RFC and never mutates RFC hierarchy; direct SR and RFC links remain independent many-to-many Task context
there is no business maximum on post-creation direct Task relationships; the database partial unique index enforces at most one active exact pair
closed relationship rows preserve historical provenance; reopening the same pair creates a new link row, never converts the closed row back to active

Objective SR/RFC/Device/Customer context remains a live derived union through current Task authority with source_task_id/link provenance; this command creates no Objective-level relationship and never mutates Objective membership, pinned plan, envelope, execution or review evidence
Device Reference regularization preserves device_reference_id, so a Task relationship remains attached to the same Device Reference rather than silently moving to a Network Element
